what_is_supported: thujone amount must be specified and daily exposure kept below the monograph limit of 6.0 mg
what_is_not_supported: does not define safety of every wormwood chemotype or essential oil; not a parasite-efficacy claim
required_next_evidence: quantified product assay and product-specific exposure assessment

what_is_supported: ACTs are the recommended treatment framework for confirmed malaria and use an artemisinin derivative with a partner drug
what_is_not_supported: does not support teas tablets capsules or crude Artemisia material for malaria treatment or prevention
required_next_evidence: quality-assured clinical treatment and resistance surveillance

what_is_supported: study-specific in vitro/in vivo Leishmania findings with reported host controls
what_is_not_supported: does not establish human dose clinical efficacy or camphor-only causality
required_next_evidence: standardized formulation pharmacokinetics and clinical safety

what_is_supported: chemotype and preparation must be reported before translation
what_is_not_supported: does not justify pooling oils or inferring safety from another species or extraction method
required_next_evidence: validated chemical assay toxicology and exposure modeling

material_or_product: Artemisia annua tea and dried-leaf preparations
active_or_marker: artemisinin plus extract phytochemicals affecting CYP2B6/CYP3A4
what_is_supported: tea and dried-leaf matrix can inhibit CYP activity and alter artemisinin exposure in human microsomes and rodents
what_is_not_supported: does not identify the responsible constituent or define a safe human dose; exposure findings are not clinical efficacy
required_next_evidence: product-specific chemical fingerprinting and human pharmacokinetic/drug-interaction assessment

what_is_supported: human volunteer study quantified artemisinin exposure after a defined 9-g dried-leaf tea preparation
what_is_not_supported: does not establish tea as equivalent to modern artemisinin drugs or support self-treatment
required_next_evidence: quality-assured product testing and controlled clinical evidence

what_is_supported: 13-week rat study reported no obvious treatment-related toxicity at 0.125-2% extract and estimated a study-specific NOAEL at or above 1.27 g/kg/day in males and 2.06 g/kg/day in females
what_is_not_supported: does not establish human safety or cover thujone-rich chemotypes and essential oils
required_next_evidence: quantified thujone exposure and species-appropriate toxicokinetic and clinical safety studies

active_or_marker: alpha- and beta-thujone plus chemotype markers
what_is_supported: authenticated and commercial oils showed substantial composition variability and thujone-associated insect behavioral and toxicity endpoints
what_is_not_supported: does not define human exposure limits or prove vermifuge selectivity
required_next_evidence: lot-specific GC-MS authentication, thujone quantitation, and mammalian toxicokinetics

material_or_product: Artemisia absinthium essential oil and extracts
what_is_supported: a low-thujone oil had negligible trans-thujone in the reported sample and was chemically distinct from thujone-rich products
what_is_not_supported: does not make all wormwood oils low-thujone or establish safety at therapeutic doses
required_next_evidence: independent lot authentication and dose/exposure-linked mammalian safety studies

what_is_supported: validated LC-MS quantitation can detect low artemisinin and identify likely contamination or misattribution in Artemisia material
what_is_not_supported: does not establish efficacy or certify botanical identity and potency beyond the measured analyte
required_next_evidence: voucher-linked multi-analyte quality control and chain-of-custody testing

what_is_supported: one Saudi oil showed a defined volatile profile and low cytotoxicity in the reported assays
what_is_not_supported: does not establish species-wide safety or extrapolate cell-assay findings to oral human use or anthelmintic selectivity
required_next_evidence: lot-specific composition plus mammalian exposure and repeated-dose studies
